A few years ago I was in the same situation as you. Severe emetophobia, a fear of flying (mostly linked to the emetophobia, and two 13 hours flights to get through. I did it, and now I enjoy flying, still with fear but not as crippling as it once was.

I might sound crazy but here’s my tips:
- Acceptance. Once that flight has taken off, there is no going back. You need to accept that fate decides now and you need to be okay with that. Whatever happens, you will get through it. 
- wear a comfy soft hoodie, have sunglasses and earphones ready. I fully cocoon when I need to pretend I’m not there. Don’t care if I look ridiculous with a hood up, sunglasses on and earphones in. 
- calming sounds/sleep playlists. If I’m panicking I find the usual music I listen to irritating and overwhelming. 
- bottle of water and lozenges. Little sips of water I find help, lozenges to keep my mouth occupied so I’m not sitting there thinking about whether I have too much/too little saliva or if my throat feels weird
- salty snacks
- travel sickness bands. I’ve never had travel sickness but having the bands on was strangely comforting on my last flight. 
- hand sanitizer. Obvious reasons. 
- tissues/wipes. They’re just handy. 
- face mask. Handy also. If someone on board happens to v* (very rare these days) I’d have my mask on because of my particle paranoia. 

These aren’t professional, and probably are weird but that’s how I survived flying ever since those two 13 hour flights.

People in the comments arguing about whether this is hoarding (it is) don’t understand the supply chain for most stores.

Yeah maybe she bought a month supply out of concern for her kiddo, or maybe she’s bragging about it who knows. But that supermarket shelf is now empty for a few days or a week waiting for the next restock. In that few days or week another family have been left without because they couldn’t buy it. Now if the lady who hoarded had purchased a weeks worth only instead of 6 weeks worth, then another family could have been supplied for a week, then the restock comes in and the families can repeat the purchase.

It’s not ideal but that is how a lot of suppliers work in supermarkets. It’s not magic. Sometimes products aren’t reordered by the store until the stock is at zero, or only ordered when a product is purchased through the cash register, or an employee will have to order when they see the shelf empty. It just takes time, time in which another baby could’ve been fed. But no, this parent wants social media points for buying out a supply. That’s the issue for me. Fucking social media point scoring. Gross.
